newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr on RBI purchases.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends down vs dlr on RBI purchases.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended Monday down against the dollar after heavy spot-dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), dealers said.
The rupee ended at 35.78/79 per dollar, off an intra-day low of 35.80 but down from the weekend close of 35.75/755.
Trades during the day ranged between 35.75 per dollar and 35.80, dealers said.
They said the day's exchange rate movement was dictated by RBI dollar purchases, with little other trade done.
"The RBI was buying quite heavily today," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "They started at 35.755 and went up to 35.795."
Dealers were unsure of the amount of central bank dollar purchases, with estimates ranging from $150 million to $300 million.
"Given today's movement in the exchange rate, their (RBI) buying must have been quite heavy," said a dealer.
Dealers said dollar supply remained good and the rupee would remain buoyant against the US currency in the short term unless the RBI continued its intervention.

"The problem is of lack of dollar demand," said the treasury head of a private bank. "Even today, despite RBI buying the rupee ended up from an intra-day low as there was good dollar supply at higher levels."
Some dealers said the central bank's Monday buying could have been with an eye on Wednesday's bond auction.
The RBI auctions 30 billion rupees of three-year federal government bonds on May 28.

"Today's spot-dollar purchases will result in rupees flowing into banks on Wednesday," said a dealer. "This will compensate for outflows towards the bond auction and should prevent any sharp rise in call money rates."
The Indian rupee ended marginally up against the forward dollar on strong supply, dealers said.

"Forward premiums opened around the weekend closing levels and eased later in the day on receiving pressure (selling of forward dollars to receive premium)," said a dealer. "Easy call money should keep premiums in check."
Forward premiums were likely to be range-bound between 4.5 percent and 5.0 percent over the short term, the dealer said.
"Supply and demand is well matched with corporates selling whenever premiums edge up," he said.
The annualised premium for six-month dollars ended Monday at 4.75 percent against the weekend close of 4.87 percent.
